newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-GUS mail order revival will be long haul.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-GUS mail order revival will be long haul.

text.p: Britain's market leader in home shopping Great Universal Stores Plc reported its first annual profit fall in nearly half a century on Thursday and said no quick fix was seen for its sluggish mail order business.
The news prompted a near seven percent fall in its share price as analysts cut profit forecasts.

GUS, also retailer of the classic Burberry raincoat, reported a two percent fall in underlying profits to 549.1 million pounds ($913 million) and said things were only marginally better since the year end despite efforts to stem declining mail order sales.
GUS said shifting its home shopping business towards high-growth direct mail and away from the declining agency market would be a long haul.
GUS shares dropped 43 pence to 622 pence after a low of 609,and retail analysts scaled back profit forecasts for the current year.

They said the drop in the shares also reflected disappointment that GUS had not taken more radical action to combat mail order's troubles. And the absence of a special dividend payout, which some investors had expected, added to gloomy sentiment about the stock.

Chairman Lord Wolfson of Sunningdale told a news conference GUS was testing four direct mail catalogues this year -- one selling Disney products, a Thomas Burberry catalogue, a specialised sportswear catalogue and Style Plus for larger size clothes.
"The likelihood is we will look at the outturn this autumn then decide where we go from here," he said.
Wolfson said agency mail order, where agents get commission for securing orders, was still viable, but this sector of the market was in long term decline.

The bulk of GUS's home shopping is via "big book" 1,200 page catalogues selling a vast range of merchandise, but smaller more upmarket niche catalogues, which now dominate the market in the United States, are now on the up in Britain.

GUS's rivals, including Marks and Spencer Plc and Burton Group Plc, are already moving into direct mail. Fashion chain Next Plc has seen sales from its home shopping Directory business grow even faster than its stores.
Wolfson said GUS did have the advantage of a ready made mail order infrastructure, but was now looking for a product that would appeal to the middle market.
"Purchasing power is going to the middle market. You have to have an offer to appeal to the middle market."
Wolfson, who took control of deeply conservative GUS last summer, said there were no plans for major acquisitions or other corporate activity.

The company bought U.S. credit information group Experian for $1.7 billion last year, a deal which was followed by other acquisitions and a property joint venture with British Land Plc . This uncharacteristic flurry of corporate activity had raised hopes there was more in the pipeline.

Wolfson noted suggestions that GUS should spin off its Burberry classic clothing business, but said a year when it had reported flat profits was probably not the time to do it. Burberry's operating profits slipped to 61.7 million pounds from 62.8 million.

He said he was not particularly wedded to the current shape of the group, which he described as a conglomerate of six separate businesses, including retailing, financial services and information services. But it was not easy to change things quickly.
"The shape of the group is not easy to change overnight," he said.

He said a special dividend was not on the agenda at the moment either. Wolfson said GUS, which paid out 300 million pounds via a special dividend in 1995, had no urgent need to offer another one as it had found other uses for its cash.
But he said if the cash began to pile up and GUS could see no more potential for acquisitions then there could be an argument for another special payout. ($ = 0.601 British Pounds)
